plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, aiming for lower drawdown. Returns are modest, but risk is substantially mitigated.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Trim CRWD to 10% to reduce single name concentration.
Buy NVDA and MRVL at 5% each, adding strong scanner setups.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small leveraged ETF presence.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding high-quality tech names. Expect moderate drawdowns with a blend of stability and growth potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Add to SOXL and SPAL, increasing leveraged ETF exposure to 6% each.
Buy NVDA and MRVL at 10% each, concentrating in high-scoring scanner setups.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases leverage and concentration in high-beta names. Be aware of higher potential drawdowns and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs; strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, CRWD, and SMH to zero, eliminating leveraged ETFs and high-beta names.
Trim SPY to 20% and QQQ to 10% to reduce growth exposure and meet mandates.
Add significantly to QQQI, prioritizing income and covered-call ETFs.
This plan focuses on steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, aiming to park cash for yield. It prioritizes steady distributions and low drawdown by rotating into income ETFs. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in selloffs; this is not a savings account.
